result:
Round 211 is planned and dispatched: it is PERF-FADER-b, which makes dragging the Clip Gain fader fast for one clip and for a multi-clip selection. My decision is **CONTINUE**. I didn't touch any store source; the tree at `180dd2e` is clean and the frozen-file check passes.

**Round 210:** C passed all 13 rows in a real browser, and gate 210 published `180dd2e` to both remotes.
- Track, group and master Volume and Pan now re-render 1 component per mouse move instead of 80–85.
- Behaviour, undo labels and the exported WAV are identical to the previous build.
- PERF-FADER-a is marked done; SABA-B-5 part 1 (the fix for those four faders) is complete.
- C found one Low (C-R210-01): doc 163 still describes the old perf-row modes. It is fixed in round 211.
- Root did not update doc 165's status line at publication. That is the fifth time this has happened, so I logged it for the next retrospective and round 211 fixes the line.

**Round 211, Clip Gain (SABA-B-5 part 2):**
- **Why:** Clip Gain is now the slowest fader. Today each mouse move re-renders 95 components, and it takes 26.5 ms stopped / 61.2 ms playing to paint (1× CPU).
- **Design:** during a pointer drag the context writes an override, the live per-clip gain and per-clip draft values. Nothing goes into undo history until release, which writes one entry. Keyboard, typed input and both resets work exactly as today.
- **Waveform:** it still grows and shrinks while you drag, as it does now. Removing that feedback in a performance round would be a visible change, so I kept it.
- **Budget:** at most 3 components per move for one clip, and N + 1 for a selection of N clips.
- **Traps the consults flagged, now explicit rules:**
  - an early return that would leave a stale value on screen when you drag back to the start;
  - two places that rebuild playback without the override (`startGraph` l.951, the playback-sync setter l.1142);
  - the exact formula for the live gain value;
  - the reset button's enabled/disabled state, which today changes mid-drag and must keep doing so.
- **Harness:** a new members scenario is added. 12 Clip Gain perf rows change from recorded to asserted. Every existing row must keep its round-210 value, except `load.components`, which may rise by exactly the number of new components the fix adds.
- **Grants:** 14 files may change and 4 new files are allowed; 1,041 files are frozen. My scan of tests that read state mid-drag matched tech-lead's independent scan line for line, and none of those reads is in a frozen file. Frozen and new-file test names were checked with `ls`.
- **Small fixes in the same round:**
  - doc 165's status line is corrected;
  - doc 163's lines are corrected (C-R210-01);
  - `withMixOverride` is no longer exported, which also closes an older deferred Low.

**Other bookkeeping:**
- **Recorded late:** the approved open-source queue changes were never logged, so I recorded them as D-29z194. PERF-6 is dropped, PERF-16 moves to right after PERF-1b, and OSS-LIC follows the first new dependency. No zustand this stage; PERF-8/10 migrate the store later.
- **Architecture review:** I committed to writing the frontend-architect review request at the next planning, whatever round 211's result. `ArrangementContext.tsx` has carried four straight rounds on one owner.
- **Schedule:** the regression round is not due until 2026-10-30, and the next retrospective is at round 215. No Critical or High finding is open.

Advisor and both consults (tech-lead, performance-optimizer) were available and used. The advisor's end review caught the two gaps that would likely have failed the round: the `load.components` change and the reset-button state. Both are fixed in the task.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- current-task.md
- tasks/round-210.md
- b-round-210.md
- b-next.json
- backlog.json
- feature-status.md
- b-round-210-r211-*.txt
- b-round-210/
